body: So to verify, the dropdown's selected value flips to `1` when BrowserAnimationsModule is present (otherwise it stays selected as is) correct?
Correct, the value flips. Removing the BrowserAnimationsModule solves the issue. Using a third-party-select like the angular/material-select dos not show the issue.

I have made a stackblitz for this bug, since the original plunkr-exmaple does not load anymore:
[https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-animations-dropdown-bug](https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-animations-dropdown-bug)

(Using angular 7.0.1)

I am having a problem with BrowserAnimationsModule (by just loading it/not using it), ngx-formly and selects.
When options are loaded a second time and there is no model for a select, the first option is choosen. 


See https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-sg8rfv?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.module.ts with the steps to reproduce.

Since Jan 23, 2018 this issue is moved to the backlog, will it be checked again by occasion?

I spent a lot of time debugging before I figured out that this issue was caused by the presence of `BrowserAnimationsModule`. Here's a simple demo illustrating the bug in Angular 8: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-bam-select-bug?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.module.ts.

Why does the animation module break select dropdowns like this? I started having this issue after adding an Angular Material component to my app, which depends on the animations module.

There are multiple Stack Overflow questions stemming from this bug:
* https://stackoverflow.com/questions/47905849/select-dropdown-displays-element-that-is-not-selected
* https://stackoverflow.com/questions/45420803/options-appearing-in-untouched-select-input

Using my StackBlitz example, I opened the Firefox dev tools and set a breakpoint on DOM mutation of the select element subtree, as well as a breakpoint in the select_control_value_accessor `writeValue` method. Normally, the code to remove the submitted option element from the DOM runs before the `writeValue` method. However, when `BrowserAnimationsModule` is present, the order is reversed, and the submitted option element isn't removed until after `writeValue` is called. This makes the `writeValue` call pointless, as subsequent modification of the option elements overrides the select element value.

Is there a bug in `BrowserAnimationsModule` that causes the order of operations to change, or does it change the order intentionally? It certainly seems like a bug for the module to change behavior like that even when no animations are being used.

issue.title: fix(forms): improve select performance and ensure that selected option matches the ngModel value

labels.name: area: core
labels.description: Issues related to the framework runtime

labels.name: target: major
labels.description: This PR is targeted for the next major release

labels.name: area: dev-infra
labels.description: Issues related to Angular's own dev infra (build, test, CI, releasing)

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Milestone for triaged issues that have not yet been scheduled for resolution.

issue.body:
Fixes #41330, fixes #14505, fixes #18430.

## PR Checklist
- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type
What kind of change does this PR introduce?
- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?
Currently Angular calls the `writeValue()` over and over for every individual option element that is added or removed from the DOM. This results in exponentially more `_compareValue` calls than the number of option elements (issue #41330).

Furthermore, calling `writeValue()` when rendering individual option elements causes an issue in Safari and IE 11 where the first option element fails to be deselected when no option matches the select ngModel. This is because Angular sets the select element's value property before appending the option's child text node to the DOM (issue #14505).

Finally, the current behavior causes an issue with delayed element removal when using the animations module (in all browsers). When a selected option is removed (so no option matches the ngModel anymore), Angular changes the select element value before actually removing the option from the DOM. Then when the option is finally removed from the DOM, the browser changes the select value to that of the first option, even though it doesn't match the ngModel (issue #18430).

## What is the new behavior?
Rather than calling `writeValue()` over and over for individual option elements that are added/removed from the DOM, call it once after all the options have finished rendering via the `afterNextRender` function. This dramatically improves performance and results in correct behavior across all supported browsers.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?
- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

issue.title: (impact: high) vcd-form-select loses selection upon changing options

repository.name: vmware-cloud-director-ui-components
repository.description: VMware Cloud Director UI Common Components

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

-   [x] Are you running the latest version? yes
-   [x] Did you perform a basic issue search?

### Description

Upon receiving a new `.options` array, the `vcd-form-select` component visually resets to the first option but the underlying [formControl] value remains with the previous selection.

I did a bit of research and it seems [this line](https://github.com/vmware/vmware-cloud-director-ui-components/blob/d54996eeaf8a94f5c9d28b50848622ebbb91588c/projects/components/src/form/form-select/form-select.component.html#L17) should use [ngValue] instead of [value]. Alternatively, adding trackBy to the ngFor may also solve it. 

It seems the problem stems from this [long standing angular issue](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/18430) between the `BrowserAnimationsModule` and HTML `select` elements. It affects all angular versions below 14.

The [stackblitz link](https://stackblitz.com/edit/base-angular-12-app-tbkkvq?file=src%2Fapp%2Fwith-ng-value%2Fwith-ng-value.component.html,src%2Fapp%2Fwith-ng-value%2Fwith-ng-value.component.ts,src%2Fapp%2Fwithout-ng-value%2Fwithout-ng-value.component.ts,src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.html,src%2Fapp%2Fwithout-ng-value%2Fwithout-ng-value.component.html,src%2Fapp%2Fapp.module.ts,src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.ts) demonstrates the problem in Angular 12, and how using [ngValue] may fix it.

### Impact

It is misleading to the user when the form input displays a different value from what is actually selected.

In our use case, the user has a table with many `vcd-form-select` components pointing to the same options. Upon refreshing the options it looks to him like all his selections were lost (even though they weren't)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Provide `vcd-form-select` with a set of initial options and a [formControl]
2. Select any option except the first one
3. Trigger a method that changes the options to a new array of equal options (equal, however not the same object references)
    example: `options = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(options))`

Observe: The form.value is still the same, but visually it looks like the first option is now selected.
Expected: Both form.value and the selection to remain unchanged.

[Stackblitz link](https://stackblitz.com/edit/base-angular-12-app-tbkkvq?file=src%2Fapp%2Fwith-ng-value%2Fwith-ng-value.component.html,src%2Fapp%2Fwith-ng-value%2Fwith-ng-value.component.ts,src%2Fapp%2Fwithout-ng-value%2Fwithout-ng-value.component.ts,src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.html,src%2Fapp%2Fwithout-ng-value%2Fwithout-ng-value.component.html,src%2Fapp%2Fapp.module.ts,src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.ts) contains a demo using the native `select` element, but `vcd-form-select` behaves exactly the same it wraps the former.

### Versions

* Angular 12
* Clarity angular 12
* @vcd/ui-components 12.0.1-dev.1

### Stackblitz

[Stackblitz demo](https://stackblitz.com/edit/base-angular-12-app-tbkkvq?file=src%2Fapp%2Fwith-ng-value%2Fwith-ng-value.component.html,src%2Fapp%2Fwith-ng-value%2Fwith-ng-value.component.ts,src%2Fapp%2Fwithout-ng-value%2Fwithout-ng-value.component.ts,src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.html,src%2Fapp%2Fwithout-ng-value%2Fwithout-ng-value.component.html,src%2Fapp%2Fapp.module.ts,src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.ts)

issue.title: fix(forms): improve select performance and ensure that selected option matches the ngModel value

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Milestone for triaged issues that have not yet been scheduled for resolution.

issue.body:
Rather than calling `writeValue()` over and over for individual option elements that are added/removed from the DOM, this change only writes to the value when it could actually be affected. This only happens when the currently selected item is changing (updated value or deleted) or if there is _no_ currently a selected value and an option value changes (either via creation or a value update). We defer the update until after rendering is complete for two reasons: first, to avoid repeatedly calling `writeValue` on every option element until we find the selected one (could be the very last element). Second, to ensure that we perform the write after the DOM elements have been created (this doesn't happen until the end of change detection when animations are enabled).

This is needed to efficiently set the select value when adding/removing options. The previous approach resulted in exponentially more `_compareValue` calls than the number of option elements (issue #41330).

Finally, this PR fixes an issue with delayed element removal when using the animations module (in all browsers). Previously when a selected option was removed (so no option matched the ngModel anymore), Angular changed the select element value before actually removing the option from the DOM. Then when the option was finally removed from the DOM, the browser would change the select value to that of the first option, even though it didn't match the ngModel (issue #18430). Note that this is still somewhat of an application issue. The model value still needs to be updated to a valid value when the selected value is deleted or it will be out of sync with the DOM.

Fixes #41330, fixes #18430.
